1. Purpose
This note documents the validation of the Copperline building-airflow case archived at /Projects/CFDME-2025-0
33_Copperline_HVAC/Case/system_archive/CPL_buoyant_case_setup.txt. Validation is performed
against tracer-gas and anemometer measurements collected in the occupied space of the Copperline municipal
building during a two-week deployment of field instruments conducted in advance of task order
TO-004 (run batch 4, executed 2025-08-14). Its purpose is to record — for internal audit, peer review, and any
subsequent reuse — the physical regime under which the archived case has been shown to reproduce the field data,
and the envelope within which the "validated" designation applies.
Nothing in this note is a validation of the archived case outside that envelope. Reuse outside the envelope described
in Section 5 requires fresh validation.

2. Case Description
The archived case is a steady, incompressible-approximation OpenFOAM setup representing interior building airflow
at municipal-HVAC supply conditions. The relevant physics elements are:

• Solver. buoyantSimpleFoam — steady, single-fluid, single-phase air, buoyancy handled via the Boussinesq
approximation (density held at ρ■; the buoyant body force is ρ■·β·(T − T_ref)·g). Pressure–velocity coupling by
SIMPLE with under-relaxation.

• Turbulence. RAS with the standard k–ε closure. Standard wall functions on all no-slip walls (kqRWallFunction,
epsilonWallFunction, nutkWallFunction).

• Supply inlet. fixedValue boundary at the diffuser face, uniform velocity magnitude 0.4 m/s along the diffuser
normal, supply temperature 293.15 K (20 °C).

• Sources. fvModels and fvOptions carry no active entries. No heat-release, chemistry, mass, or momentum
sources are applied. No chemistryProperties dictionary is loaded. No combustion model is present.

• Radiative transport. No radiationProperties dictionary is loaded. No fvDOM, P1, or viewFactor entries
are present anywhere in the case. No radiation model is present. Interior air at the design supply state is
optically thin over the room scale.

• External envelope walls. Adiabatic. zeroGradient on temperature, fixedFluxPressure on p_rgh, noSlip
on velocity. No through-wall conductive or radiative flux is modelled.

• Schemes. steadyState ddt; first-order upwind on the advected scalars (T, k, ε) and on the momentum
equation; corrected Laplacian; linear interpolation.

• Time control. endTime = 2000 SIMPLE iterations; adjustTimeStep inactive; writeControl timeStep.
The solve is steady; no physical time integration is performed.
The case is a small-perturbation buoyant HVAC solve. It is not a reacting-flow case, not a radiation-participating case,
and not a transient case.

3. Validation Data
Two independent instrument streams were recorded in the occupied space of the Copperline municipal building over
a two-week deployment (2025-07-28 through 2025-08-10), with the data used subsequently to support
the case under task order TO-004 (executed 2025-08-14):

• Tracer-gas measurements. SF■ decay measurements taken from four sampling ports distributed across the
primary occupied zones (open bullpen, conference room north, conference room south, corridor). Injection
followed a step-release protocol; concentration decay was logged at 30-second cadence over each decay run.
Twelve decay runs were captured across a range of nominal supply-fan settings.

 • Anemometer readings. Hot-wire anemometry at nine fixed monitoring stations placed at seated breathing height
(1.1 m AFF) in the occupied zone. Sample rate 1 Hz; each station logged continuously for the two-week window.
Reported values are 10-minute rolling means at steady supply-fan conditions.
Instrumentation was owned and operated by Copperline facilities under Nadia Okoro's coordination. Anemometer
calibration certificates and the SF■ analyzer service record are filed alongside the raw data logs. All measurements
were taken in a period of stable supply-air temperature (variation across the two-week window bounded within ±3 °C
of the design setpoint).

4. Comparison
The archived case was solved on the geometry of record for the occupied space, with the supply boundary set at the
0.4 m/s nominal condition documented in Section 2, and simulated velocity magnitude and predicted zone-mean
tracer decay were compared to the field observations.

• Velocity magnitude, anemometer stations. Simulated velocity magnitude at each of the nine anemometer
stations agrees with the measured 10-minute-mean values within 12% across all stations.

• Tracer decay. Predicted SF■ decay in each of the four sampled zones agrees with the measured decay curves
within 8% on the fitted decay constant.
Both agreement bands are inside the acceptance targets adopted for building-airflow validation on this project and
are consistent with the k–ε RAS closure and first-order upwind discretisation used. Detailed per-station and per-zone
tables are in the case's validation/ subdirectory.

5. Validated Envelope
This validation applies only within the envelope: INTERIOR BUILDING AIRFLOW, STEADY, isothermal to within 6
degC, inlet velocities 0.2-0.8 m/s, no combustion model and no radiation model present, ceiling and wall boundary
conditions adiabatic. Extension to reacting flows, buoyancy-DOMINATED flows, or wind-driven EXTERNAL flow
requires re-validation. Validated status does not transfer across regimes.
The following regime attributes are load-bearing on the "validated" designation above and cannot be assumed to hold
outside the envelope:

• The flow is interior building airflow. External-flow physics — atmospheric shear, wind-driven pressure loading,
terrain roughness, atmospheric boundary-layer inlets — is outside scope.

• The solve is steady. Any transient phenomenon — including plume puffing, fire-induced entrainment, or unsteady
buoyant instability — is outside scope.

• The temperature field is isothermal to within 6 °C of the supply setpoint. Boussinesq closure is not asserted
outside this band.

• The supply velocity magnitude sits inside the band 0.2-0.8 m/s. Values outside this band are outside scope and
re-validation is required before the case is used at any other supply setting.

• No combustion model is present or asserted. The case carries no chemistry, no heat-release source, and no
reaction closure. Any reacting-flow problem is outside scope.

• No radiation model is present or asserted. The case carries no radiationProperties and no
participating-media transport. Any radiatively-driven problem is outside scope.

• Envelope walls are adiabatic. Through-wall conduction and any coupled envelope-thermal problem is outside
scope.
Any extension outside the above — reacting flows, external wind-driven flow, buoyancy-dominated regimes
(Froude/plume-velocity ratio away from HVAC values), non-isothermal problems, or supply-velocity operating points
outside 0.2-0.8 m/s — requires re-validation under the governing modeling standard (rev 4 §7). The "validated"
designation attaches to this case within this envelope only; it does not attach to the directory, to the file names, or to
the mesh, and it does not transfer across physical regimes.

6. Reviewer Sign-off
The validated envelope stated in Section 5 above governs any reuse of this case; extension outside that envelope
requires re-validation.

reviewed against the firm's modeling standard rev 4 and against the QA verification standard. The case is accepted
as validated within the envelope stated in Section 5. Reuse of this case in any other physical regime is not authorised
on the basis of this note.

against the wind-tunnel measurements of record for the airframe geometry and freestream conditions covered by the
Dry Wash SOW. It records the comparison of computed and measured surface pressure coefficients across the
operating envelope, states the envelope in which the case is validated, and states the conditions under which that
status does not transfer.
The output of this memo is a validated status attached to a specific case within a specifically bounded envelope. It is
not a certification of the geometry, the solver, or any directory containing the case files. Reuse outside the stated
envelope requires re-validation per firm modeling standards.

terms in fvOptions. There is no radiation model present or exercised.

• surface or gas temperature measurements,
• heat flux measurements,
• any reacting-flow scalar (species mass fractions, heat-release rate, radiant intensity),

 • any buoyancy-driven quantity.

steps.message:
I have prepared and saved the resolution-basis disposition note at `/filesystem/CFDME-2025-041_resolution_note_revA.docx`. Below is a summary of the findings from the existing file-server artifacts (`CFDME-2025-041_Phase1_report_revB.docx`, `CFDME-2025-041_scoping_memo_20251008.docx`, `Case/verification/three_grid_study_outputs.txt`, `Case/logs/log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt`, `Case/logs/log.solve_20251009_attempt3.txt`, `Case/system_archive/OAS_case_setup_from_DWA.txt`, and `Data/site_met_avra_valley_2015-2024.csv`).

---

### 1. Where the Plume Resolution Index Lands, Underlying $dx$ and $D^*$, and Band Compliance
* **Result the report rests on:** The preliminary LES plume-dynamics and thermal results in Phase 1 Report rev B (§5.3–§5.4: puffing frequency $0.87\text{ Hz}$ / period $1.15\text{ s}$, $T_{\text{peak}} = 1461\text{ K}$, $U_{z,\text{peak}} = 12.4\text{ m/s}$ at $t = 40.0\text{ s}$, and Pope resolved-TKE fraction $84\%$ [$0.84$] in Appendix C) come from the **fine grid (`case_fine`, $11{,}196{,}000\text{ cells}$)** of Renata Ellsworth’s fluid-only three-grid LES verification study (`Case/verification/three_grid_study_outputs.txt`), which §6.3 selects as the reporting grid and whose Level 3 ($dx = 0.5\text{ m}$) plume-core target spacing matches the $11{,}214{,}862\text{-cell}$ multi-region conjugate production mesh (`Case/logs/log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt`). The six SOW §3.1 production conjugate-heat-transfer LES runs are deferred to Sprint 2 (`2025-10-20`); the only solver run log on the production mesh (`Case/logs/log.solve_20251009_attempt3.txt`) is Mulshi Simulation Labs’ stalled steady-state RANS ($k\text{--}\varepsilon$, SIMPLE) bring-up attempt at $240^\circ$ and $8.0\text{ m/s}$.
* **Plume length scale ($D^*$):** From the Sonoran buffelgrass fuel model ($w = 0.6\text{ kg/m}^2$, $h = 18{,}600\text{ kJ/kg}$, Rothermel spread rate $R = 0.9\text{ m/s}$), Byram fireline intensity is $I = h \cdot w \cdot R = 10{,}044\text{ kW/m}$, rounded to $10{,}040\text{ kW/m}$ (Byram flame length $L = 5.4\text{ m}$). Over the $L_{\text{segment}} = 3.0\text{ m}$ fire-front sub-domain segment, total heat release rate is $\dot{Q} = 10{,}040\text{ kW/m} \times 3.0\text{ m} = 30{,}120\text{ kW}$, rounded to **$\dot{Q} = 30.1\text{ MW}$ ($30{,}100\text{ kW}$)**. Using QA Verification Standard rev 3 §2:
  $$D^* = \left(\frac{\dot{Q}}{\rho_\infty c_p T_\infty \sqrt{g}}\right)^{2/5} = \left(\frac{30{,}100\text{ kW}}{1.204\text{ kg/m}^3 \times 1.005\text{ kJ/(kg}\cdot\text{K)} \times 293.15\text{ K} \times 3.13209\text{ m}^{1/2}\text{/s}}\right)^{2/5}$$
  gives an exact unrounded value of **$D^* = 3.7423\text{ m}$** ($3.7433\text{ m}$ at $30{,}120\text{ kW}$), rounded in Scoping Memo §5.1 and all downstream logs/tables to **$D^* = 3.76\text{ m}$**.
* **Cell size ($dx$), plume resolution index ($D^*/dx$), and band compliance ($5 \le D^*/dx \le 10$ per QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5.1):**
  * **On the reporting basis ($dx = 0.5\text{ m}$ fine-grid background / Level 3 plume-core target):** $D^*/dx = 3.76\text{ m} / 0.5\text{ m} = \mathbf{7.52}$ (reported as **$7.5$** in Scoping Memo §5.1 and Report Appendix C Table 6, and **$7.52$** in the verification and meshing logs; **$7.48$** unrounded). **The firm’s $[5, 10]$ band is met** at the midpoint of the band ($+2.52$ margin above $5$; $2.48$ margin below $10$). (On background $dx$, the medium grid at $dx = 0.7\text{ m}$ lands at $5.37$ [inside band] and the coarse grid at $dx = 1.0\text{ m}$ lands at $3.76$ [below band].)
  * **On the local refined near-source zones ($dx = 0.25\text{ m}$ and $dx = 0.125\text{ m}$):** In `three_grid_study_outputs.txt` (and Report §6.2), the cylindrical `fireRefinementZone` ($1{,}256{,}640\text{ cells}$ on `case_fine`) carries two additional refinement levels above background ($dx_{\text{ref}} = 0.5\text{ m} / 2^2 = 0.125\text{ m}$), and in `log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt` (base $L_0 = 4.0\text{ m}$), `refinementBox_plume` is Level 4 ($dx = 0.25\text{ m}$) while the region within $3.00\text{ m}$ of `OAS-WUI-01_revC_plumeSource.eMesh` is Level 5 ($dx = 0.125\text{ m}$). Evaluated at those local refined cell sizes, $D^*/dx$ lands at **$15.04$ ($15.0$)** at $dx = 0.25\text{ m}$ and **$30.08$ ($30.1$)** at $dx = 0.125\text{ m}$ ($14.97$ and $29.94$ unrounded), which **exceed the upper limit of $10$** (classified by §5.1 as compute over-refinement rather than insufficient resolution).

---

### 2. What Our Resolution Acceptance Rests On & What Needs a Decision from Marguerite
* **Basis of acceptance (`CFDME_QA_Verification_Standard_rev3.pdf` §§4–6):**
  * Roache/Richardson GCI is strictly prohibited for LES (§4) because narrowing the LES filter width shifts the resolved-to-subgrid turbulence split (explaining the non-monotonic monitor shifts across Coarse, Medium, and Fine in Report Table 4: $T_{\text{peak}} = 1420\text{ K}, 1487\text{ K}, 1461\text{ K}$ and $U_{z,\text{peak}} = 12.8\text{ m/s}, 11.2\text{ m/s}, 12.4\text{ m/s}$).
  * Under §5 (*"Either alone is acceptable; both are preferred"*), LES resolution acceptance rests on meeting either or both of: (1) **§5.1 Plume resolution index** $5 \le D^*/dx \le 10$ (met at **$7.52$** on the $dx = 0.5\text{ m}$ plume-core target mesh), and/or (2) **§5.2 Pope resolved-TKE fraction** $k_{\text{res}} / (k_{\text{res}} + k_{\text{sgs}}) \ge 80\%$ ($0.80$) time-averaged over $\ge 10$ puffing cycles inside the buoyancy-dominated flow (met at **$84\%$ [$0.84$]** on `case_fine`, $+4\text{ percentage points}$ above the $80\%$ threshold, averaged over $t = 8.0\text{ s}$ to $40.0\text{ s}$ [$32.0\text{ s} \approx 27.8\text{ puffing cycles}$ at period $1.15\text{ s}$]).
  * Because the $11{,}214{,}862\text{-cell}$ multi-region production mesh ($z_{\text{top}} = 40\text{ m}$, 5 `cellZones`) has not yet been solved in transient LES, acceptance for Phase 1 rev B rests on carrying over these metrics from the fluid-only `case_fine` verification mesh ($11{,}196{,}000\text{ cells}$, $z_{\text{top}} = 60\text{ m}$).
* **Four items requiring a decision from Marguerite (as Reviewing Engineer under §5 and §7):**
  1. **Governing $dx$ convention ($0.5\text{ m}$ background/$L_3$ vs. $0.25\text{ m} / 0.125\text{ m}$ local refinement shells):** Confirm whether $dx = 0.5\text{ m}$ (matching Scoping Memo §5.1 counter-signed by Marguerite on `10/08/2025`) is accepted as the governing $dx$ for $D^*/dx = 7.52$ (inside $[5, 10]$), OR, if local refined $dx = 0.25\text{ m}$ ($D^*/dx = 15.04$) or $0.125\text{ m}$ ($D^*/dx = 30.08$) is treated as the fire-region $dx$, accept the mesh under §5 via the **"either criterion alone is acceptable"** provision (resting acceptance of the $0.125\text{ m}$ zone on Pope’s $84\% \ge 80\%$ criterion) and/or a §5 Reviewing Engineer escalation approval because 2-to-4-level mesh grading is geometrically required to transition from the $0.5\text{ m}$ plume core to the $50\text{ mm}$ concrete leaves ($L_6 = 62.5\text{ mm}$) and $3.8\text{ mm}$ steel ties ($L_7 = 31.25\text{ mm}$) per Modeling Standard rev 4 §6.
  2. **Probe-zone alignment for the $84\%$ Pope resolved-TKE figure:** Decide whether to accept the paired metrics with explicit disclosure in Section 6 ($D^*/dx = 7.52$ verifying the $dx = 0.5\text{ m}$ outer plume core and $84\%$ Pope resolved-TKE verifying the inner $dx = 0.125\text{ m}$ refined fire-source zone), or rest acceptance of the $0.5\text{ m}$ zone on $D^*/dx = 7.52$ alone under §5.
  3. **Fluid-only verification study carryover to the un-run conjugate production mesh:** Confirm that the fluid-only `case_fine` study (`three_grid_study_outputs.txt`) closes the mesh-resolution basis on the $11{,}214{,}862\text{-cell}$ production mesh ahead of the Sprint 2 (`2025-10-20`) production conjugate LES runs.
  4. **Standard reference vs. site ambient properties in $D^*$:** Confirm that retaining $D^* = 3.76\text{ m}$ from the signed scoping memo is accepted with the site-condition sensitivity ($D^*/dx = 7.27\text{--}7.79$) documented in Section 6.

---

### 3. Whether the Resolved-Energy Figure Was Taken Inside the Index Region & Effect of Site Conditions on $D^*$
* **Was the $84\%$ resolved-energy figure taken inside the region the index describes?**
  * **Physically (buoyancy-dominated plume core per §5.2) — YES:** The probe is on the plume axis at $z = 0.75\,D^* = 0.75 \times 3.76\text{ m} = \mathbf{2.82\text{ m}}$ above the source top surface ($2.81\text{ m}$ exact; $z = 2.92\text{ m}$ AGL given the $0.10\text{ m}$ height of `OAS-WUI-01_revC_plumeSource.eMesh`). Because $2.82\text{ m}$ lies within $1.0\,D^*$ ($3.76\text{ m}$) and well below the $5.4\text{ m}$ Byram solid-flame length (with $T_{\text{peak}} = 1461\text{ K}$ and $U_{z,\text{peak}} = 12.4\text{ m/s}$), it sits directly inside the active buoyancy-dominated reacting plume core per §5.2.
  * **Grid-wise (against the $dx = 0.5\text{ m}$ cell region described by $D^*/dx = 7.52$) — NO:** At $z = 2.82\text{ m}$ above the source top surface ($< 3.00\text{ m}$ from `plumeSource`), the probe sits inside the two-level-refined fire-source zone in both meshes (`fireRefinementZone` in `three_grid_study_outputs.txt` and the $3.00\text{ m}$ Level 5 distance shell around `plumeSource.eMesh` in `log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt`), where the local cell size is **$dx = 0.125\text{ m}$** (local $D^*/dx = 30.08$), not in unrefined $dx = 0.5\text{ m}$ cells.
* **Do the ambient values behind $D^*$ represent the site, and what would site conditions do to it?**
  * **No:** $\rho_\infty = 1.204\text{ kg/m}^3$, $T_\infty = 293.15\text{ K}$ ($20.0\,^\circ\text{C}$), and $c_p = 1005\text{ J/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$ are standard $20.0\,^\circ\text{C}$ sea-level reference properties ($101.32\text{ kPa}$), not the Avra Valley Sonoran Desert WUI site envelope ($T_\infty = 35\text{--}42\,^\circ\text{C}$ [$308.15\text{--}315.15\text{ K}$], RH $10\text{--}25\%$, elevation $\sim 750\text{ m}$ with $K_e \approx 0.92$ / $p_{\text{site}} \approx 92.6\text{--}93.2\text{ kPa}$, and nominal site density $1.2\text{ kg/m}^3$ in `windload_basis_memo.pdf` §2.1a & §5; nor the non-compliant Dry Wash Aerospace high-altitude values $\rho_\infty = 0.4\text{ kg/m}^3, T_\infty = 223\text{ K}, p_\infty = 26{,}500\text{ Pa}$ archived in `OAS_case_setup_from_DWA.txt`, which would yield $D^* = 6.48\text{ m}$ and $D^*/0.5\text{ m} = 12.97$).
  * **Effect of Avra Valley site conditions on $D^*$ and $D^*/dx$:**
    1. **Updating $T_\infty$ to $35\text{--}42\,^\circ\text{C}$ ($308.15\text{--}315.15\text{ K}$) at fixed $\rho_\infty = 1.204\text{ kg/m}^3$ (or $1.20\text{ kg/m}^3$):** Since $D^* \propto T_\infty^{-2/5}$, $D^*$ **decreases by $1.97\%$ to $2.85\%$**, from $3.76\text{ m}$ ($3.742\text{ m}$ exact) to **$3.67\text{--}3.69\text{ m}$** at $35\,^\circ\text{C}$ ($3.668\text{ m}$ exact / $3.686\text{ m}$ scaled; $3.673\text{ m}$ at $\rho_\infty = 1.20\text{ kg/m}^3$) and **$3.64\text{--}3.65\text{ m}$** at $42\,^\circ\text{C}$ ($3.636\text{ m}$ exact / $3.653\text{ m}$ scaled; $3.640\text{ m}$ at $\rho_\infty = 1.20\text{ kg/m}^3$), lowering $D^*/dx$ (at $dx = 0.5\text{ m}$) to **$7.27\text{--}7.38$**.
    2. **Consistent ideal-gas adjustment at constant sea-level pressure ($101.32\text{ kPa}$):** Heating air to $35\text{--}42\,^\circ\text{C}$ lowers $\rho_\infty$ proportionally to **$1.145\text{--}1.120\text{ kg/m}^3$**, keeping the denominator product $\rho_\infty T_\infty = p_\infty / R_{\text{air}} = 352.95\text{ kg}\cdot\text{K/m}^3$ invariant and leaving **$D^* = 3.742\text{ m}$ ($3.76\text{ m}$ reported) and $D^*/dx = 7.48\text{--}7.52$ unchanged**.
    3. **Consistent ideal-gas adjustment including the $\sim 750\text{ m}$ Avra Valley elevation ($p_{\text{site}} \approx 92.6\text{--}93.2\text{ kPa}, K_e \approx 0.92$) and $T_\infty = 35\text{--}42\,^\circ\text{C}$:** Lower barometric pressure reduces $\rho_\infty$ to **$1.047\text{--}1.054\text{ kg/m}^3$** (at $35\,^\circ\text{C}$) and **$1.024\text{--}1.030\text{ kg/m}^3$** (at $42\,^\circ\text{C}$), decreasing $\rho_\infty T_\infty$ by $8.0\text{--}8.6\%$ and **increasing $D^*$ by $+3.39\%$ to $+3.65\%$** to **$3.87\text{--}3.90\text{ m}$** ($3.869\text{--}3.879\text{ m}$ exact / $3.888\text{--}3.897\text{ m}$ scaled), which raises $D^*/dx$ (at $dx = 0.5\text{ m}$) to **$7.74\text{--}7.79$**.
    * **Net result:** Under all site-condition formulations, $D^*/dx$ at $dx = 0.5\text{ m}$ stays within **$7.27\text{ to }7.79$**, well inside the firm’s $[5, 10]$ acceptance band.

---

### 4. Whether Checklist Item 4 Can Close & What Would Settle It
* **Can Item 4 close right now on Phase 1 Report rev B as drafted? NO.** Even though the numerical LES resolution metrics exist on the file server, Section 6 ("Verification") of `CFDME-2025-041_Phase1_report_revB.docx` violates QA Verification Standard rev 3 §§3–6 and Modeling Standard rev 4 §§5 & 8 by placing a RANS-style three-grid table (Table 4) in the body, relegating $\dot{Q}$, $D^*$, $dx$, $D^*/dx$, and the Pope resolved-TKE fraction to Appendix C via an appendix pointer in §6.3, omitting the LES sub-grid-scale (SGS) closure (WALE or Dynamic Smagorinsky) and the §3(d) single-sentence margin statement, and leaving the mesh-zone, site-condition, and fluid-only carryover caveats undocumented.
* **What will settle and close Item 4 without running anything new:**
  1. **Promote the Appendix C LES resolution metrics into the Section 6 Verification body** (placed ahead of Results and Validation per §3), explicitly stating all five mandatory §6 quantities with units ($\dot{Q} = 30.1\text{ MW}$ [$30{,}100\text{ kW}$; $30{,}120\text{ kW}$ unrounded], $D^* = 3.76\text{ m}$ [$3.742\text{ m}$ exact; $3.64\text{--}3.90\text{ m}$ at site conditions], $dx = 0.5\text{ m}$ plume-core target with local $0.25\text{ m}$ [$L_4$] and $0.125\text{ m}$ [`fireRefinementZone` / $L_5$] shells and cell counts $11{,}196{,}000$ / $11{,}214{,}862$, $D^*/dx = 7.52$ [$7.5$; $7.27\text{--}7.79$ at site conditions], and Pope resolved-TKE $= 84\%$ at the plume-axis probe $z = 0.75\,D^* = 2.82\text{ m}$ above the source top surface over $t = 8.0\text{--}40.0\text{ s}$ [$\ge 20$ puffing cycles at $0.87\text{ Hz}$ / $1.15\text{ s}$]).
  2. **Demote Table 4 (the three-grid monitor comparison)** from Section 6 to Appendix C, explicitly titled as an *"Informational Mesh Sensitivity Study (No GCI Computed)"* per QA Verification Standard rev 3 §4 and §6.
  3. **Add the mandatory §3(a), §3(d), and Modeling Standard §8 statements to Section 6:** state the LES turbulence treatment and SGS closure (WALE or Dynamic Smagorinsky), cite `CFDME_QA_Verification_Standard_rev3` and `CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4`, and include the §3(d) single-sentence acceptance-and-margin statement.
  4. **Record Marguerite’s Reviewing Engineer concurrence on the file-server basis** (that under §5, $D^*/dx = 7.52$ verifies the $dx = 0.5\text{ m}$ outer plume core while Pope resolved-TKE $= 84\% \ge 80\%$ verifies the inner $dx = 0.125\text{ m}$ refined fire-source zone with §5 escalation concurrence for wall/tie mesh transition grading, and that the fluid-only `case_fine` verification study settles the mesh-resolution basis for the $11{,}214{,}862\text{-cell}$ production mesh ahead of Sprint 2). *(Note: Closing Item 4 clears the resolution-basis item; final signature on Phase 1 Report rev B under Checklist Item 10 will still require closing the remaining open non-resolution checklist items: Items 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, and 9.)*
